dateline: Hawthorne, CA / Boca Chica, TX — May 2002–Present
heroHeadline: June 1: 'Starfall' Reentry Program Revealed + IPO S-1 Amended — 68th Mission & OCISLY's 200th Landing; Roadshow in 3 Days
heroSubtitle: 8,791 days since SpaceX founding — June 1, 2026 opened with three headline developments: FAA environmental documents reveal SpaceX's previously undisclosed 'Starfall' program — a reusable reentry vehicle for point-to-point cargo delivery (up to 1,000 kg, launching on Falcon 9 or Starship, two Pacific Ocean reentry zones ~1,300 km off US/Mexico coasts); SpaceX filed an S-1 IPO amendment warning investors it may issue 'significant equity' in future transactions, fueling Tesla merger speculation just 3 days before the management roadshow (June 4–8); and Falcon 9 B1088 (16th flight) launched 24 Starlink V2 Mini satellites from Vandenberg SLC-4E for the 68th orbital mission of 2026, with OCISLY achieving its 200th booster touchdown — the drone ship's second century milestone and the 619th cumulative SpaceX recovery. IPO pricing remains on schedule for June 11 with Nasdaq (SPCX) debut June 12 targeting a $75–80B raise at $1.75–2T valuation. Starlink constellation: 10,558+ active satellites, 10.3M subscribers. Starship remains grounded pending FAA IFT-12 mishap investigation (expected late June 2026); Booster 20 + Ship 40 continue integration at Starbase for IFT-13 targeting July–August 2026.
